create.name: Mysore Point CDMX
create.bio:
Mysore Point CDMX is an Ashtanga Vinyasa school in the Polanco district of Mexico City, run by Toni (María Antonieta Ortiz Colmenero) and Benji. The pair first took up asana in 2010, found the traditional Ashtanga method in 2014 and have travelled to India repeatedly since 2016 to study with Sharath Jois; Toni holds Level 2 authorisation from the Sharath Yoga Centre in Mysore.

The school keeps the classical format. On weekday mornings the room is open from early until nine, and students of every level arrive within that window to work through their own sequence, learning it a few postures at a time with the teachers' help; a led class follows on Saturdays, and moon days are kept as rest days. Beginners need no prior experience, and first sessions last around three quarters of an hour. Toni and Benji also teach private Mysore-style classes at students' homes, alone or in small groups, and the school's blog places the practice within Patanjali's eight limbs, presenting the Mysore method as a practical route into the Yoga Sutras. Teaching is in Spanish.

courses.title: Mysore class packages
courses.description: Passes for the weekday Mysore room and the Saturday led class, from a single class to an unlimited month, with introductory first-week and first-month offers for new students.
courses.price: Primera semana $550; Primer mes $1500 (new students); Mes ilimitado $3,000; 10 clases $2,700; Clase suelta $320

courses.title: Clases privadas (private Mysore-style classes)
courses.description: Mysore-style teaching brought to the student's home, either one to one or for a small group of family or friends, following the same progressive approach as the school's morning room.

free_resources.title: Aṣṭāṅga Vinyāsa yoga: Un modelo práctico del Yoga de Patañjali
free_resources.description: A Spanish-language article by Toni on the history and philosophy behind Ashtanga, the eight limbs set out in Patanjali's Yoga Sutras, and how daily Mysore practice can carry those teachings into ordinary life.
